grātīs

adverb · Wiktionary

free of charge, for nothing

Contracted from grātiīs, the form of Plautus and Terence (Lewis & Short). “It costs nothing” is grātīs cōnstat (Sen. Ep. 104.34; Cic. Verr. 2.5.48, Lewis & Short); to give away free, grātīs dare (Mart. 14.175.2, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • grātuītus, grātuīta, grātuītum — free, given without payment

    adjective · classical · Suet. Cal. 26: grātuīta in Circō loca, free seats (Lewis & Short); Cic. Leg. 1.48 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Free as against paid for: free seats, an interest-free loan (pecūnia grātuīta, Plin. Ep. 3.11.2, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nōn potest grātīs cōnstāre lībertās

    freedom cannot be had for nothingSen. Ep. 104.34

  • et tantum grātīs pāgina nostra placet

    and my pages only please when they are freeMart. 5.16.10

See also free, cheap, expensive, how much is it?, cost a lot.
